title: bug: chat_who and chat_join compute presence inline instead of isWorkerAlive, skipping its DEAD test, so a seat deregistered moments ago (or a DEAD seat still parked in chat_wait) is listed online; chat_join's copy also drops every live IDLE seat, against its own MCP_SERVER.md note
description:
Filed by the governor from hunt #14's held items (task-d5d58972, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-1656a684). Re-verified at HEAD d5431577.

PROBLEM
packages/moe-daemon/src/util/workerLiveness.ts:15-21 defines isWorkerAlive as "The ONE predicate for 'is this worker alive'": not DEAD, and lastActivityAt within LIVENESS_TIMEOUT_MS. It says it is "Shared by listWorkers, chat_who and the sweeps... Do not re-implement this check inline." Two chat tools do re-implement it:
- chat_who (tools/chatWho.ts:6, :51-53) has its own PRESENCE_TIMEOUT_MS and checks lastActivityAt only. A DEAD record with recent activity is listed. Its Pass 2 (:82-108) also lists any worker parked in chat_wait, DEAD included.
- chat_join (tools/chatJoin.ts:62-69) requires `status !== 'IDLE' && recent`. So it lists a just-deregistered DEAD seat and omits every live IDLE seat. docs/MCP_SERVER.md's `### moe.chat_join` note says "Online workers are those with activity within the last 120 seconds", with no IDLE exclusion. Its own code comment says "active status or recent activity".
- list_workers already uses isWorkerAlive, so a seat list_workers reports isAlive:false shows as online in chat_who.

EVIDENCE
Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/zzHuntA_chatWhoDead.test.ts, run at HEAD 942717bc in a snapshot; output in chatWhoDead.vitest.txt. Right after deregister_worker, list_workers reports isAlive:false, while chat_who returns `worker-closed:DEAD` in online. The code is unchanged at d5431577.

FIX DIRECTION
Make both tools call isWorkerAlive, with the shared LIVENESS_TIMEOUT_MS, and drop the inline constants.
- chat_who's Pass 2: keep "parked in chat_wait counts as present", since a long wait does not refresh activity, but never for a DEAD record.
- chat_join: choose between the doc's rule (every live seat) and the IDLE exclusion, and make the code and its `### moe.chat_join` note agree.
Sync both sections, `### moe.chat_join` and `### moe.chat_who` (ruling msg-71db57ac): online means not DEAD and active within 120 s, or (chat_who with a channel) parked in chat_wait.
Error handling is unchanged.

FILES AND PLACEMENT
tools/chatWho.ts, tools/chatJoin.ts, one vitest file, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md (those two sections only). The sibling row filed alongside this one fixes updateWorkerCursors (workerStore.ts). The two are independent: there is no dependsOn and no shared file. Gate: that vitest file, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail).
definitionOfDone: chat_who (with and without a channel, including a DEAD worker parked in chat_wait) and chat_join never list a DEAD worker. A vitest case deregisters a recently active seat and checks both tools.

A live IDLE seat that list_workers reports isAlive:true is listed by both tools. If chat_join keeps an IDLE exclusion, its `### moe.chat_join` note documents it instead, and the test pins whichever rule ships.
Both tools take presence from isWorkerAlive (no inline PRESENCE_TIMEOUT_MS left in chatWho.ts or chatJoin.ts), and the two MCP_SERVER.md sections state the same rule.

implementationPlan.description:
Both tools take presence from isWorkerAlive (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/workerLiveness.ts:15-31: not DEAD and lastActivityAt within LIVENESS_TIMEOUT_MS; the predicate list_workers reports as isAlive).
(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatWho.ts:
- import `isWorkerAlive` from '../util/workerLiveness.js' and delete the module constant PRESENCE_TIMEOUT_MS (:6);
- Pass 1 (:51-53): replace the inline lastActivity computation and its check with `if (!isWorkerAlive(worker, now)) continue;`;
- Pass 2 (:96-98): a worker parked in chat_wait counts as present even past the window, because a long wait does not refresh activity, but never a DEAD record. Change `if (worker)` to `if (worker && worker.status !== 'DEAD')`. Never upgrade a DEAD record either: Pass 1 already skipped it, so it cannot be in `seen`.
(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatJoin.ts (:62-71): import isWorkerAlive. Replace the inline loop's condition with `if (isWorkerAlive(worker, now))` and delete the local PRESENCE_TIMEOUT_MS.
- Chosen rule: the DOC's. Every live seat is online, IDLE included, so the `status !== 'IDLE'` exclusion goes. Its own comment ('active status or recent activity') and `### moe.chat_join` already describe that rule, and no consumer reads onlineWorkers (grep: only chatJoin.ts and the doc).
- Rewrite the comment to name isWorkerAlive.
Do not touch mentionRouter.ts: its IDLE/DEAD filter (:244-249) picks notification targets, not presence, and its comment documents that.
Error handling: unchanged. Neither tool gains a new throw, and the channel and worker validation stay first. Edit with the seat's own editor (Serena or Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec), never a shell write.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: chat_who and chat_join take presence from isWorkerAlive: not DEAD, and active within LIVENESS_TIMEOUT_MS (120 s). That is the predicate list_workers reports as isAlive. A just-deregistered DEAD seat is never listed, even with recent activity or a lingering chat_wait waiter. chat_join lists live IDLE seats, as its doc says. chat_who with a channel still lists a live worker parked in chat_wait past the window. Both MCP_SERVER.md sections state the same rule.

No consumer reads onlineWorkers: only chatJoin.ts and the doc mention it.
The existing chatChannelRef and workerType suites pass unchanged (dry run).

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- activeChatWaiters is a module-level Map exported from chatWait.ts. Tests seed it directly and must clear it, and the timers, in afterEach.

- A leftover activeChatWaiters entry, or its setTimeout, leaks into other test files in the same worker, so clear both in afterEach.
- The structural check needs the literal `isWorkerAlive(` in both tools.
- Rails: no npm in the shared checkout, no pattern kills, and tracked files written only with the seat's own editor.
